articles.description:
I built a blackjack simulator. That sentence undersells it. What I actually built is a 28,000-line Python framework for simulating card games with an event-driven architecture, immutable state management, and realistic shuffle physics. For blackjack.
This is what happens when a software engineer gets curious about casino math.
It started the way these things always start: I wanted to understand the numbers. Not the hand-wavy "the house has a 0.5% edge" stuff you read online, but the actual mechanics. How does basic strategy change when the dealer hits soft 17? What does card counting really buy you? How many riffle shuffles does it take before a deck is actually random?
I could have read a book. Instead I wrote a simulator. Then I rewrote it. Then I rewrote it again.

articles.description:
At the start of my career as a security engineer, I built an allow list management system for our web gateway within the security operations center (SOC) I worked in. Beyond just a script, this was a live system that a core security component relied on. Someone once blocked a /3 vs a /32 IP range, and access to a third of the internet broke for all 40,000 employees. I knew the system I created had to prevent something like that from occurring again. The manager of the SOC analysts would have regular discussions with myself and my manager on any issues that arose, which helped me realize the impact my code had on someone else’s work. That was the first time I felt responsible for software, not just automation.

articles.author: Radmir
articles.description:
WebAssembly is a pretty young technology and a promising one, it has many pros (platform independent, lighter than containers) and usage scenarios (browser apps, plugin system, edge computing).
WASM is designed to be language-agnostic. However, working with it from Python as a host may be not so obvious.
Basically, WASM application consists of two parts: host and guest.
Host is the environment that runs wasm and controls its execution (e.g. a browser or a runtime like wasmtime).


Guest is the pluggable wasm module, that is built from Rust, C, Wat, Python, or whatever you want. It runs in sandboxed host environment




To simplify guest <-> host interaction, there is a tool called Wasm Interface Type (WIT) - we can just describe interfaces in .wit files and then generate bindings for both …

Until yesterday, my scripts were observers.
Today my computer started watching back.
Not scanning a target.
Watching itself.
And that’s actually what most real cybersecurity tools do.
I had a simple thought:
Malware rarely announces itself.
An attacker who compromises a machine needs communication.
Command & Control (C2) callback.
Reverse shells

They create an outbound network connection.

I decided to monitor my own machine’s network connections in real time.

Ever wondered how digital devices represent time using nothing but ones and zeros? This problem invites you to decode a binary watch, where LEDs represent powers of two for both hours and minutes. It is a fantastic way to practice how we can combine different possibilities to reach a specific target.
You're given:
turnedOn, which represents the total number of LEDs currently glowing on a binary watch.
Your goal:
The watch has 10 LEDs in total: 4 for hours () and 6 for minutes (). Since the total number of possible times is small (only  combinations), we can use a Backtracking (DFS) approach to pick which LEDs to turn on.
The core logic revolves around iterating through the 10 available LEDs. For each LED, we decide to "turn it on" and subtract 1 from our turnedOn count. We keep track of th…
